translation.text: It will be known to you that the Most High will remember your destruction, and the angels of heaven will rejoice over your ruin.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected opening is a known/be-known construction, not an independent statement that something will come upon you. The object of remembering is your destruction, not a silently substituted your sins. The following angels rejoice over your ruin. The source’s star before angels is preserved in the source transcription; no reported variant is adopted here.

translation.text: All the matters of your unrighteousness will be read before the Great Holy One,[a] and your faces will be put to shame. He will reject every work firmly established in unrighteousness.[b]

The final work clause, not the facial-shame phrase, carries the firm/established expression. Primary lexical ranges support rejection and firmness, but exact selected forms remain held for further font review. The English does not add a new personal identification for the Great Holy One or replace the work clause from a later English edition.

translation.text: Woe to you, sinners in the midst of the sea and on dry land, whose remembrance is evil against you.[a]

translation.text: Now let us do what we have planned, for we have gathered silver and filled our storehouses like water, and the cultivators of our households are many.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected speech is first-person plural: let us, we have planned, we have gathered, and our storehouses and houses. Silver is explicit, not a substituted generic wealth noun. The selected text has like before water; no reported alternative supplies an extra conjunction there. Cultivators preserves the agricultural sense of the final starred noun, rather than unrestricted laborers or an asserted slave class. Households renders the source’s houses expression; no new place, crop or estate size is inserted.
